sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: The latest available announcement batch is Friday, 6 November 2026; this daily report uses that prior batch because Monday's batch was not yet available. Fourteen notable papers are included: nine new submissions or cross-list entries and five substantive revisions. Computational biology and AI are being judged with more explicit validation: experimental follow-up, held-out benchmarks, reliability measures, or dynamical checks. Spoken agenda: agent-led drug discovery, single-cell models and their limits, and the difference between prediction and validation.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a readership ranking. Much clinical and experimental biology appears outside arXiv.

sections.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
sections.abstract: PharmAgents2 combines literature-derived decision skills and parallel agent exploration, reports a 121-question benchmark, and describes three discovery investigations whose findings were subsequently tested by human researchers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say PharmAgents2 connects scientific decision support with parallel exploration; reported scenarios include LpxH inhibition, JAK1 candidate testing, and experimental support for a secondary-target binding result.
sections.unique_caveat: These are early research scenarios, not clinical evidence. The authors say JAK1 selectivity and binding modes need further validation; the LpxH site and mechanism remain to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three author-reported wet-lab follow-ups and a 121-question benchmark with three end-to-end tasks; Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations and 0 influential citations at snapshot.

sections.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
sections.abstract: BILBY-PRO broadens motif-scaffold evaluation to 220 PROSITE-derived cases, while BILBY-MD tests whether static designs retain motif and scaffold behavior in molecular-dynamics simulations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 31/55 model–problem solves met their MD-support threshold, but only 8/55 passed all checks, showing static recovery does not establish whole-scaffold dynamical fidelity.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors call the MD thresholds heuristic and note 200 ns trajectories may miss slower instability; MD support does not establish biochemical function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track); evaluates six generators and 220 benchmark cases, then dynamically assesses 55 static solves. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
sections.abstract: MUSS combines DNA-derived peak and gene representations with paired single-cell chromatin-accessibility and expression data to predict regulatory readouts, including for unseen genomic regions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report strong results against sequence and single-cell baselines, including prediction for held-out genes and peaks, using a frozen AlphaGenome encoder and multiscale peak–gene interactions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is benchmark-based computational evidence, not direct experimental confirmation of regulatory mechanisms. The authors note encoder dependence, paired-data requirements, quadratic attention cost, and limited multi-seed testing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Journal reference: NeurIPS 2026; evaluates four paired datasets and tests held-out sequences/cell types plus other regulatory tasks. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Thalamus-Reasoning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Multi-Sample Omics Reasoning
sections.abstract: The revised Thalamus-Reasoning model encodes bulk or single-cell transcriptomes as continuous embeddings for language-guided analysis across multiple samples.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report leading results on several held-out annotation tasks and GEO-OmicsQA variants, plus best average performance on PerturbQA among compared methods.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is on curated computational tasks, not experimental discovery; some training supervision is LLM-generated, with task-specific quality checks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v3 revision; GEO-OmicsQA has 3,000 publication-disjoint questions. Semantic Scholar reports 1 citation and 0 influential citations, current totals only.

sections.title: scTREAT: Latent Diffusion for Single-Cell Drug-Response Prediction
sections.abstract: The revised scTREAT model uses latent diffusion with explicit cell-state, drug-identity, and dose conditioning to predict single-cell drug-response profiles.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report best scores on 10/12 metrics for unseen cell-line–drug combinations and 11/12 for unseen drugs among tested methods.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational evaluation on condition-level pseudobulk profiles; predicted responses require independent experimental validation and are not treatment evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v3 revision evaluated on Tahoe-100M condition-level profiles. Semantic Scholar reports 8 citations and 0 influential citations, current totals only.

sections.title: One Method Does Not Fit All: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Imputation Methods for Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data
sections.abstract: The revised benchmark compares 16 scRNA-seq imputation methods across protocols, tasks, and datasets, finding that relative performance depends on the analytical setting.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that traditional methods are often more consistent across tasks, and better numerical recovery does not necessarily improve biological interpretation.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors find no universally best method; benchmark comparisons do not show that imputation recovers true expression in every setting.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v3 revision; covers 16 methods, 10 protocols, six downstream tasks, and 30 benchmark datasets. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Querying Counterfactuals on Tissue Graphs with Supervised Disentanglement
sections.abstract: Cellina separates intrinsic cell state from spatial context to model in-silico tissue-neighborhood interventions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stronger in-silico perturbation predictions than spatial and non-spatial competitors and identify cancer subdomains with distinct predicted signaling programs.
sections.unique_caveat: Counterfactual outputs are predictions, not newly performed interventions; benchmark performance does not establish causal validity in other tissues.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v4 revision; benchmarks span more than 2.5 million spatially resolved cells. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Reclassification Is All You Missed: Surfacing Variant Reinterpretation Need in Online Health Communities at Population Scale
sections.abstract: PRISM screens public health-community posts for possible genetic-variant reinterpretation needs and drafts, but does not send, outreach after checking later ClinVar classifications.
sections.claimed_contribution: PRISM surfaced 123 candidate classification differences, five from uncertain to pathogenic or likely pathogenic, in a no-contact dry run.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a clinical service or evidence that recontact improves outcomes; factual grounding alone did not make all drafted messages suitable to send.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Analyzes 3.9 million posts across 32 communities; a clinician assessed 30 held-out drafts, judging 27 grounded and 15 fit to send. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
sections.abstract: An audit of perturbation-response models finds a low-rank decoder and proposes nearest-neighbor distance from predicted responses as a confidence signal for prediction accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose predicted-nearest-neighbor distance as a per-prediction reliability estimate and report transfer across evaluated encoders and cell lines.
sections.unique_caveat: Tests cover a limited set of models and perturbation settings; confidence-score correlation does not validate predictions experimentally or establish performance in new biological settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026; tested across three encoders and four CRISPRi cell lines, with reported mean absolute Spearman correlation 0.81. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: High resolution 3D localization of ultrasound sparse sources using a SAGE algorithm
sections.abstract: A SAGE-based estimator localizes simultaneous sparse ultrasound sources, reporting 0.24 mm error in simulations and improved resolution on proton-induced nanodroplet-vaporization data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose parametric localization for transient simultaneous sources and report better spatial resolution than beamforming in their experiment.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is simulation plus a specific experimental dataset, not a patient study or clinical validation of proton-therapy monitoring.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Includes 49 simulated acquisitions and experimental ultrasound-array data, with sub-millimeter agreement reported against the proton distribution. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
sections.abstract: A North West London primary-care study finds colorectal-cancer discrimination rises modestly as an EHR model's lookback expands to 18 years, then plateaus.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report AUROC rising from 0.551 at two years to 0.590 at 18 years, then plateauing; XGBoost reached 0.589.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective single-region evaluation with modest discrimination; no prospective utility is shown, so this is not a validated screening test.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at ML4H 2026 Findings; evaluates a frozen cohort of 1,008 cases and 9,582 matched controls. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.comment: Accepted at Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026, Findings Track.

sections.title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort
sections.abstract: This revised MRI study tests whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before ComBat estimation reduces residual scanner association in glioma radiomic features.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report residual scanner association in 13/428 features after standard ComBat versus 8/428 after batch-augmented ComBat.
sections.unique_caveat: Single-center harmonization results do not establish external generalization or improved patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 revision; retrospective 733-patient, single-center cohort across nine scanner configurations; journal reference to JMRI 2026. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.comment: Original article. Submitted to Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (JMRI).

sections.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
sections.abstract: A fixed-budget DiffDock study finds focused supervision on geometrically consequential corrections does not consistently improve pose success over broad continuation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report broad continuation had the highest mean trained-policy Top-1 success below 5 Å; focused or mixed supervision showed no consistent gain under the tested budget.
sections.unique_caveat: This result is specific to DiffDock and the tested supervision choices and budget; it does not show focused supervision cannot help elsewhere.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop; compares multiple supervision policies and distinct pose-quality measures. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop.

sections.title: Accelerating reaction network identification via frequency-domain analysis
sections.abstract: For certain stochastic reaction systems, the authors find Fourier-domain likelihoods can be approximately Gaussian and use that observation to speed Bayesian network inference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present frequency-domain inference intended to reduce the computational burden of particle-filter-based Bayesian identification for a subset of systems.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract demonstrates one gene-transcription example; behavior across broader reaction-system classes remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.MN submission with a gene-transcription example. Semantic Scholar: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Single-cell models increasingly represent or evaluate more than a gene list: MUSS grounds peaks and genes in DNA sequence; Thalamus-Reasoning and scTREAT integrate transcriptomes with language or drug context; the imputation benchmark compares methods across 30 datasets; and Cellina models spatial context. A second recurring motif is evaluation design: BILBY adds dynamics beyond static protein recovery, docking separates score fidelity from pose success, and the perturbation audit asks when predictions are reliable. Validation levels vary sharply: PharmAgents2 reports wet-lab follow-up, ultrasound combines simulations with a specific experiment, PRISM has clinician review but sends no messages, while several other papers are computational and the EHR/MRI studies retrospective.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Replicate PharmAgents2 hypotheses with blinded, orthogonal target-engagement assays, off-target panels, and independent-lab follow-up. Test portability of MUSS, Cellina, Thalamus-Reasoning, scTREAT, and imputation models on unseen donors, labs, cell types, mechanisms, tissues, and sequencing platforms, with independent assays. For BILBY, pair longer matched-reference simulations with experimental folding, binding, or catalytic tests across motif/context classes. Before any variant-recontact use of PRISM, assess privacy and consent, clinician escalation, correction channels, and message comprehension in an independently reviewed external cohort. Test colorectal prediction and MRI harmonization across health systems and scanners before clinical-use claims.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: This batch's strongest signal is methodological: papers test when predictions survive broader datasets, alternative metrics, physical simulation, or experimental checks. PharmAgents2 reports the clearest wet-lab bridge, while single-cell and medical-model updates remain computational or retrospective. These preprints do not establish clinical benefit; independent replication and external validation are next.
